note: BBVA Perú only: BCP's site sits behind Cloudflare, Interbank's refused the request (403) and Scotiabank Perú's card page wasn't found; the SBS's interest-rate and transparency pages sit behind Incapsula. BBVA Perú's summary sheet for its Visa and Mastercard credit cards (version September 2026), read in full: the five cards it sells, Cero BBVA, Bfree, Platinum, Signature and Black, in soles. Each carries a fixed effective annual rate (TEA, on a 360-day base) on purchases, revolving or in instalments (the Black's priced from 39.99% to 69.99%, written at the top), and 104.99% on cash; the rate is effective, so a month charges the rate that, compounded twelve times, makes it. The annual membership (none on the Cero) is waived when the card's purchases average a stated sum a month (200 soles on Bfree, 800 on Platinum, 2,000 on Signature and Black), written as twelve times that over the year; the Black's waiver for the PRIME segment isn't written. A cash withdrawal at another bank's ATM or a counter costs 4% (at least 20 soles, at most 50); the Cero's at the bank's own ATMs costs nothing and isn't written. Currency conversion costs 3% on transactions abroad in a currency other than the US dollar, written as the foreign transaction fee. The moratory interest (12.51% nominal a year on soles debt) is charged on top of the compensatory rate and isn't written as a penalty rate; the sheet's minimum payment of at least 30 soles appears only in a worked example and isn't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Scotiabank Perú, one of the country's four largest banks, whose tariff page links one tariff per card: its sixteen personal cards' tariffs (changes in force from 13 October 2026), read in full (the Jockey cards, two cards on one sheet laid out in columns that don't separate, and the business cards aren't written). Each card, in soles: an effective annual rate (TEA, 360-day base) on purchases from 19.99% to the sheet's top (112.99% on most, 109.83% on the AAdvantage Clásica, 79.99% on the Singular Infinite), written at the top with 19.99% as the range's lowest; its top effective rate on cash; the annual membership, priced in US dollars and written at the soles figure the sheet gives beside it at its reference rate of 4.00 soles to the dollar (none on the Visa Sin Membresía); a cash withdrawal at a local ATM of 4.5%, at least 15 soles and at most 50 (the bank's own network, web and app cost nothing, which isn't written); and a 3.00% currency conversion charge on transactions abroad in a currency other than the US dollar, written as the foreign transaction fee. The moratory interest (11.78% nominal a year on soles debt on most cards) is charged on top and isn't written as a penalty rate, as for BBVA; no minimum payment, grace period or late fee is stated. Tried and not used: BanBif's site sits behind Cloudflare (403); Banco Pichincha Perú's, Mibanco's and Banco Ripley Perú's home pages answered but weren't searched for a tariff in this pass; Banco Falabella Perú's tariff page loads its documents by script and gives none to a plain request, and Diners Club Perú's site links no tariff.
